title: Kitforge SDK manifest + snippet index (draft)
content:
Summary:
A compact, opinionated SDK starter kit (codename: Kitforge) intended for fast internal prototyping and external first-touch demos. Focus is on: minimal friction, consistent microcopy, reusable snippet primitives, and a 10-minute ‘first success’ quickstart that works with the Redwood hosted API and a local mock.

Goal:
- Reduce time to first meaningful SDK call to <10 minutes for engineers unfamiliar with Redwood APIs.
- Provide a single, small importable package of copy+snippets that other teams can embed in docs, quickstarts, and interactive lab notebooks.
- Standardize telemetry hooks and failure messaging so the DX team can quickly triage field issues.

Target personas:
- New backend engineer (open-source library user): wants fastest path to a generation sample and cost estimate.
- Frontend engineer integrating streaming chat: needs clear sample for streaming + fallback.
- Solutions engineer preparing a customer demo: wants one-liner deploy and a canary checklist.

Scope / non-goals:
- Scope: sampleapp scaffolds, guided microcopy, 8–10 curated snippets (JS/Python), small CLI for local mock + smoke tests, and an index.md reference for copy variants.
- Non-goal: full SDK API rewrite or major runtime features. Kitforge should shim to existing client libs.

Kit components (proposed):
1) Quickstart (10-min): a single-file example that does: auth setup, simple text generation, streaming output (if available), and a token cost preview call.
2) Microcopy studio: canonical strings for onboarding screens, error banners, and rate-limit messages (with short, empathetic tone).
3) Snippet primitives: 8 small snippets (init, generate, chat-stream, embeddings, rerank, cache-check, warmup, graceful-fallback). JS + Python parity.
4) Local mock CLI: minimal local mock server (faststart) + smoke script that hits the quickstart example.
5) Telemetry pattern: example metrics emitted (latency, tokens_out, model_variant, failure_reason) and sample logging snippet.
6) Acceptance tests: checklist and tiny test harness to assert quickstart returns 200 + non-empty tokens.
7) Index.md: short descriptions, recommended copy per use-case, and snippet usage table.

Snippet index (short listing):
- kitforge/init-js: import, setKey, setRegion (3 lines)
- kitforge/generate-basic-py: minimal sync generate + print first 3 tokens
- kitforge/chat-stream-js: attach to browser-socket, handle partial messages + reconnect hint
- kitforge/embeds-minimal-py: call embeddings and format for vector DB
- kitforge/rerank-example-js: score list of candidates using rerank endpoint shim
- kitforge/cache-probe-py: check prefix cache header and print hit/miss
- kitforge/warmup-shell: curl script that triggers KV warm cache and returns 204
- kitforge/fallback-policy-js: policy snippet to downgrade to a cheaper model if latency>200ms

Microcopy examples (opinionated):
- Onboarding CTA: "Get your first response in seconds — create a key and run the example."
- Rate-limit banner: "We’re sending lots of requests right now. Try again in a few seconds or switch to a lower-cost model in settings."
- Error modal (user-visible): "Something went wrong fetching results. We’re retrying automatically — if the problem persists, contact us at support@redwood.ai."

Runloop manifest (developer checklist):
- [ ] Create single-file quickstart for both Py/JS (owner: Ben)
- [ ] Add mock CLI and smoke tests (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Publish microcopy variants to index.md and docs repo (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] Wire telemetry examples and sample dashboards (owner: Rae)
- [ ] Align snippet names with SDK package exports (owner: eng-sdks)

Acceptance criteria for first release (v0.1):
- Quickstart runs locally against hosted API with documented env vars and passes smoke test.
- Snippets repo has cross-language parity for core 6 snippets.
- Microcopy has been reviewed by docs and UX (two reviewers) and committed to index.md.
- Telemetry sample produces metrics compatible with the Console trace prototype.

UX & accessibility notes:
- Keep copy short (<100 chars) and use active voice.
- Provide a keyboard-focusable sample page for the streaming snippet.
- Include text alternatives for any demo visuals.

Edge cases & open questions (Notes to self):
- Q1: How opinionated should fallback model suggestions be when customers pin model versions? (DX-412 relates)
- Q2: Do we include an official TS types bundle or rely on existing SDK types? (ben wants TS-only option)
- Q3: For local mock, should we emulate KV cache headers (X-Redwood-Cache) or keep mock minimal?

Linked dev tasks (short):
- GH: PR 89 is the initial snippet scaffold (see linked_artifacts).
- JIRA: DX-412 tracks microcopy review.
- Confluence: longer design notes and canary policy examples.

Timeline proposal (week-level):
- Week 0: core quickstart + one snippet per language (prototype)
- Week 1: mock CLI + smoke tests + microcopy pass 1
- Week 2: telemetry wiring + index.md + internal review
- Week 3: public docs merge + release v0.1

Risks / mitigation:
- Risk: quickstart brittleness due to auth infra changes. Mitigation: include a local mock path and keep hosted API calls gated behind a single env var.
- Risk: fragmentation between JS/Python parity. Mitigation: continuous snippet parity check in CI (small script).

Appendix: quick copy snippets for reviewers (raw):
- "Create a free API key and paste it into REDWOOD_API_KEY. Then run: 
  node quickstart.js
  # or
  python quickstart.py
"
- Warmup note (for solutions engineering): "Run warmup before demos to populate KV cache and ensure 95th% latency is stable."

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Schedule microcopy review with docs (Aisha)
- [ ] Add smoke CI job to run mock + quickstart nightly (Priya)
- [ ] Draft a short ‘how to embed a snippet’ guide for Solutions (Rae)

Open items to discuss in next sync:
- How to label snippets in the public examples repo so they’re discoverable by non-engineers.
- Whether the quickstart should surface cost-estimate telemetry by default.

End notes: this doc is intentionally terse and actionable — it’s a scaffold to move fast. Copy variants and sample code should be treated as living artifacts; prefer small, reviewable PRs over one giant merge.
